frozenDesignInvariants.invariant: The only runtime root is com.google.crypto.tink:tink-android:1.23.0 in :poc:recovery, with the dependency-local com.google.code.findbugs:jsr305:3.0.2 exclusion.
Streaming uses AES-GCM-HKDF with 16-byte input key, 16-byte derived AES-GCM key, SHA-256 HKDF and 4096-byte ciphertext segments.
AEAD uses AES-256-GCM with 32-byte key, 12-byte IV, 16-byte tag and TINK variant.
Every generated keyset has exactly one enabled random-ID primary, constructed through the exact KeysetHandle public builder sequence.
TinkConfig.register() and the fixed RegistryConfiguration.get() remain private to the crypto boundary; callers cannot supply a weaker configuration or obtain raw primitives/keyset handles.

Encrypted keysets use only the nondeprecated four-argument TinkProtoKeysetFormat serialize/parse APIs with exact typed KeyEnvelope AAD; no cleartext keyset serialization or cleartext key material exposure exists.

Each stream run, microfile and manifest/checkpoint generation receives a fresh keyset; a new keyset must serialize its envelope before exactly one encryption, and an envelope failure permanently poisons that wrapper.
Parsed keysets are decrypt-only and no open/recovery path may generate or replace a key.
Streaming, microfile, publication and key-envelope AAD are strict REC-I1 typed codecs with target, candidate, run, generation, range, cadence and chain-digest cross-binding as applicable.
The stream envelope is generation 1, no unit, range [0,115200000), cadence 0 and zero genesis digest.

Android Keystore creation calls generateNewAeadKey(canonicalKeyUri) once then obtains the AEAD from Builder.setKeyUri(...).build().getAead(...); open-existing performs only the latter route, with no generation fallback.
Key-confirmation AEAD authentication/AAD failure remains typed separately from authenticated post-decrypt strict-codec or value mismatch; neither assigns a REC-I3 outcome.

The approved exact graph remains six runtime and two test-only artifacts, 61/61 configurations resolved, 34 policy-covered configurations free of JSR305 components and class definitions, and 27 tooling configurations separately inventoried.
Release R8 uses exactly three narrow javax.annotation dontwarn rules, no broad dontwarn, retains the crypto boundary and packages no javax.annotation definition or native/JNI entry.

This implementation remains local, unpublished and nonmetric; it includes no harness, orchestrated kill/recovery campaign, device/emulator/network execution, REC-I3 activation, PoC PASS, readiness closure or dependency/production admission.
